t: grammar - "first I go buy" or "first I go to buy" - English Language Learners Stack Exchange
s: The first is not grammatically correct; "go [verb]" is short for "go to [verb]" or "go and [verb]." The second, while there's a typo (which is obviously accidental since you spelled it right the first time), is grammatically correct. However, I would not recommend it for several reasons: It's in first person; you are writing an essay about how you make a salad, I would write it in the imperative mood (simply "First, buy the ingredients").

t: I will buy vs I’m going to buy vs I’m buying | WordReference Forums
s: October 11, 2020 - If you're just expressing intention, all three mean the same. None of them indicate spontaneity more than the others. You might choose one over the others in specific contexts. For example you might use an emphatic "will" if you mean you're definitely going to buy a computer the next day.
